title: When Drugs Stop Working
paragraphs: When an antibiotic enters the body, it kills bacteria or stops them from multiplying. Most of the bacteria die, but a few may carry small genetic differences that help them survive the drug. Those survivors then multiply, and their descendants inherit the same protection. Over many generations, a whole population can become resistant. Bacteria can also pass useful genes directly to their neighbours, which spreads resistance even faster.

This process can happen naturally, but human behaviour has sped it up. Antibiotics are often taken for colds and flu, which are caused by viruses, so the drugs do nothing except give bacteria more chances to adapt. Large amounts are also used in farming. Alexander Fleming, who discovered penicillin, warned about this danger in his Nobel lecture in 1945.

The World Health Organization now describes antimicrobial resistance as a major global threat to public health. When common drugs fail, ordinary infections become harder to treat, and routine operations become riskier. Too few new antibiotics are being developed, so experts argue that protecting the drugs we already have matters just as much. That means using them only when they are truly needed, preventing infections through clean water and vaccines, and watching carefully for resistant strains.

sources.claim: Antibiyotikler bakterileri öldürür ya da çoğalmalarını durdurur; ilaçtan sağ çıkan bakteriler çoğalarak dirençli popülasyonlar oluşturabilir ve direnç genleri bakteriler arasında aktarılabilir.
sources.source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Antimicrobial Resistance; https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/

sources.claim: Antibiyotikler virüslerin yol açtığı soğuk algınlığı ve gribe karşı etkisizdir; gereksiz kullanım direnci hızlandırır.
sources.source: U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, Antimicrobial Resistance; https://www.cdc.gov/antimicrobial-resistance/

sources.claim: Antibiyotiklerin insanlarda ve hayvancılık/gıda sektöründe yanlış ve aşırı kullanımı direnci hızlandırır.
sources.source: World Health Organization, Antimicrobial resistance (fact sheet); https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/antimicrobial-resistance

sources.claim: Alexander Fleming 1945 Nobel konuşmasında penisilinin yetersiz dozda kullanılmasının mikropları dirençli hâle getirebileceği konusunda uyardı.
sources.source: Alexander Fleming, Penicillin, Nobel Lecture, 11 Aralık 1945; https://www.nobelprize.org/prizes/medicine/1945/fleming/lecture/
